scoreReasons: Every on-chain settlement is public, with a transaction hash returned to the client, but an exact EIP-3009 payment looks like an ordinary token Transfer plus AuthorizationUsed, so nothing marks it as x402.
The x402 contracts (Permit2 proxies, batch settlement) emit named events at the same address on every supported EVM chain, which makes those paths easy to index.
Facilitator capabilities (GET /supported) and the Bazaar resource catalog are public HTTP endpoints, and x402scan publishes an explorer and API.

The richest data (requirements, resource URLs, amounts before settlement, vouchers, screening decisions) stays in headers and facilitator logs, and credit-backed cloudflare:402 commitments never reach a chain.
Public volume counters exist but are contested and were not visibly updated after 2026-08-25.

public.where: The token contract on each chain
public.how: Transfer and AuthorizationUsed events; the transaction hash also arrives in PAYMENT-RESPONSE.
Same addresses on every supported EVM chain; batch channels emit ChannelCreated, Deposited, Claimed, Settled, Refunded, WithdrawInitiated, WithdrawFinalized and ChannelClosed.
Lists kinds (x402Version, scheme, network), extensions and signer addresses per CAIP-2 family.

public.where: GET /discovery/resources and GET /discovery/search; CDP instance at api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/discovery/resources
public.how: Public listings of resources with accepts entries and lastUpdated; no API key needed on the CDP instance; no category data.

public.where: https://www.x402scan.com and its API routes (buyers, facilitators, merchants, origins, registry, resources, send, wallets)
public.how: Operated by Merit Systems; discovery reads /openapi.json with x-payment-info, then /.well-known/x402, and trusts runtime 402 behavior over static metadata.
RFC 9421 public keys for signature agents in cloudflare:402 and the http-message-signatures extension.
builder-code appends an ERC-8021 Schema 2 suffix naming app, wallet or facilitator, and service.

public.where: x402.org, GitHub Security Advisories, the repository
public.how: 30-day counters (contested), GHSA advisories, Cantina audit reports, changelogs.

private.why: They travel only between client, server and facilitator, including resource URLs, descriptions and amounts.

private.what: Facilitator logs, KYT and OFAC decisions, pending settlement stores
private.why: Operational data of each facilitator; nothing obliges publication.
Cumulative vouchers live in server storage until the server claims them on chain.

private.what: cloudflare:402 credit commitments and billing identity
private.why: Credit-backed payments never reach a chain; Cloudflare maps signature identities to accounts.
Nothing on chain links a wallet to an agent or a person, which is the root of the volume dispute.

indexerCaptures.from: Token Transfer and AuthorizationUsed events, joined with known facilitator signer addresses from /supported
x402ExactPermit2Proxy and x402UptoPermit2Proxy events at their fixed addresses
GET /discovery/resources on public Bazaar instances and x402scan registry routes
ERC-8021 builder-code suffix in settlement calldata
